Q: What's the correct term for a "diamond" in a directed acyclic graph? A:

Perhaps you could call such a subdigraph a "commutative digraph", as two or more paths from the source vertex to the target vertex commute. (For instance, see Figure 2 of this paper, and Figure 1 of this paper.)

A generalization, accommodating the possibility of parallel directed edges (sharing the same direction between two vertices) could be called "commutative multidigraph".

Q: `tr1` not known when compiling Hilo Browser in VS 2026 A:

When is_base_of was merged into the language standard, it had the same syntax that your code appears to have. It should be sufficient to remove tr1:: leaving the line as

static_assert(std::is_base_of<IUnknown, T>::value, "T needs to be IUnknown based");

This trick will likely work for most things defined in std::tr1, but if you encounter others, it would be prudent to double-check with a language reference, such as cppreference.com, in case there had been minor adjustments. (In particular, I would watch for things the compiler might miss, such as the order of template arguments.)
